newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices drop as demand slows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices drop as demand slows.

text.p: Millfeed prices were quoted lower in nearly all markets in reaction to a slowdown in demand, increased production from flour mills and the availability of new-crop corn, sources said.

In the Midwest, flour mills increased milling operations to six and seven days a week from five and six days. Flour production seasonally increases now to satisfy demand for the Thanksgiving and Christmas holiday periods.
In the Southeast, millfeed consumption by catfish was declining as the fish become less active.
Lush pastures in north Texas have curbed the need for supplemental feeding. An abundance of rain through late summer improved pastures from Texas to Kansas, dealers said.
"We have grass everywhere," said one Texas dealer.
Southern California dealers said millfeed values remained firm because of tight supplies of competing feed ingredients.
